doc.title: Allan Vaché interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 15, 2000

title: New York and Florida scenes
summary: He worked Eddie Condon's, finds New York's club scene diminished, and prefers Florida's scene.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Did you ever crack into the New York scene at all?

Well yeah, well I grew up in the New York/New Jersey area, and I worked Eddie Condon’s for quite a while, and I’ve always been kind of in and out of the New York scene even though I live in Florida. I just don’t like living in New York. It’s not one of my favorite places. And it’s not the same place I grew up in. There’s not as much going on in New York as when I was a kid in the 60s and 70s. I mean there was a lot more going on then than there is now. There’s not very much of a club scene there anymore. I mean the clubs that you do go in — you work The Cajun on 34th Street, and they pay you forty dollars. It’s really pretty sad. But most of the guys who are in the scene, I have known and I’ve worked with back in the early 70s and the late 60s, and I’ve always kept in touch with them. And a lot of the guys I work with, a lot of them are out of New York. I usually go back there once or twice a year and work some of the clubs that are in New Jersey or New York, just to keep my hand in and let everybody know I’m still around. But living in Florida too is a lot better than when I was in Texas. There’s a pretty good

scene in Florida, a lot of good players down in Florida, Flip Phillips and Bill and John Allred, a lot of great players, Johnny Varro, a lot of guys around there, so there’s a lot more going on there.
